title: prmarmot-cli board@1
description: What `prmarmot-cli mine --json`, `prmarmot-cli review --json`, and `prmarmot-cli all --json` print: one view with its PRs in display order. Within board@1 fields are only added, never renamed or removed, so ignore fields you don't know.

viewer.description: The GitHub login the board was built for.

view.description: The app's name for the view. "Involving me" is My PRs across all repositories without `--authored`. "All open" is every open PR in one repository (`all`).

sort.description: Order inside Requested from you and Available to review: `wait` (longest wait first) or `smallest` (`review --sort smallest`: size band, then changed lines, then wait; PRs without a size last). Section order never changes.

count.description: PRs listed, after filters; `count + filters.filtered_out` were loaded.

total.description: How many PRs GitHub's search matched, loaded or not. In `all`, every open PR in the repository, or with `label:` or `author:` in `--filter` the open PRs matching them (GitHub matches those two across the whole repository; other terms check only the loaded PRs). Also set for `mine`. Null for `review`, whose two searches overlap, and when GitHub did not say.

agent.description: true for `--agent` (only PRs a coding agent or bot opened), false for `--no-agent` (only a person's), null when neither was passed.

stale_after_days.description: Days of waiting that make a PR `stale` (config `stale_after_days`, default 3).

truncated.description: GitHub has more results than were loaded.

attention_state_error.description: Why the app's watch/snooze/changed state couldn't be read; `attention` then shows nothing marked.

sections.description: Non-empty sections in the app's display order: the default, or the user's `section_order` from config.toml. Find a section by `key`, not by position.

mode.description: authored: My PRs (`mine`). review: the Review queue. all: All open, every open PR in one repository; `watch` never follows it.

rate_limit.description: GitHub's GraphQL budget after the request, or null when GitHub didn't report it.

key.description: Stable key. approved: approved and waiting to merge. action: needs action: yours blocked on you (see `blockers`), or, in Involving me and `all`, someone else's with a conflict, failing CI, requested changes or unresolved comments. await: waiting on reviewers (one is requested or has commented). todo: your review is requested. available: nobody is requested yet; in Involving me and `all`, someone else's PR with no reviewer requested and no review. done: you already reviewed. draft: drafts. snoozed: snoozed in the app. In Involving me and `all`, approved, action, available, await and draft hold anyone's PRs; `author` says whose.

label.description: The app's section title; wording may change.

explanation.description: What puts a PR in this section, in one sentence: the app's hover text on the section header. Wording may change.

author.description: Null when the account no longer exists.

category.description: The PR's category, which can differ from its section's `key`: in `mine` and `all`, PRs under `approved` and `available` have category `await`. Use the section's `key` to find a section's PRs.

queue.description: Review queue, and All open's `todo`: whether your review was requested. Null in My PRs.

ci.description: The head commit's check rollup; none when it has no checks, hidden when the token may not read them (a fine-grained token never can).

merge_queue.description: The PR's entry in its repository's merge queue, or null when it is not queued. GitHub merges a queued PR when its turn comes, so the Note says "in merge queue, position N" rather than "mergeable". Absent from releases up to v0.14.0.

position.description: One-based, as GitHub shows it; null when GitHub did not say.

review_decision.description: GitHub's decision; null without branch protection that requires reviews.

review_state.description: Other reviewers' standing reviews combined: a change request outweighs approvals; waiting means reviewers are requested and nobody has reviewed.

requested_reviewers.description: Pending requests: user logins and team slugs.

reviews.description: Each other reviewer's standing review: the latest, except that a later comment doesn't cancel an approval or change request.

my_review.description: Your own standing review, by the same rule as `reviews`; NONE when you haven't reviewed.

unresolved_threads_capped.description: The PR has more review threads than the newest 100 that were read, so unresolved_threads counts only those and may be low.

issue.description: The linked issue found by the configured issue pattern.

blockers.description: Why a PR of yours is in `action`; empty elsewhere.

note.description: The app's one-line summary; wording may change.

commits_since_review.description: Commits the PR gained since your latest review, when its head moved on from the commit you reviewed; null otherwise (your own PR, no review, head unchanged, or the list not read).

lower_bound.description: The reviewed commit is older than the newest 20 read, so `count` is at least this (the Note says "20+").

waiting_since.description: Pickup age: when the PR started waiting for a reviewer (your latest review request, the longest-standing request on your PR, or when it opened or became ready for review); null for drafts and PRs already reviewed.

unresolved_paths.description: The files the unresolved review threads are on, each once, newest thread first; at most 20. Empty when no thread is open or GitHub did not say.

name.description: The check run's name or the commit status's context, as GitHub shows it.

url.description: The run's page, when GitHub gave one.

failed_checks.description: The checks on the latest commit that failed, newest first, from the newest 30 contexts; at most 10. Empty when CI is not failing or the token cannot read checks.

agent.description: Opened by a coding agent or another bot: GitHub's `Bot` account type, or an author config `agent_authors` names.

size.description: The change's size; null when GitHub did not report the counts.

band.description: small: at most 100 changed lines (additions + deletions) and at most 10 files; large: more than 400 lines or more than 30 files; medium otherwise. Lockfiles and generated files count too.

changed.description: Changed since you last selected it in the app.
